title: First Detection of CS Masers around a High-mass Young Stellar Object, W51 e2e
question: Do the CS J=1-0 and J=2-1 rotational transitions show maser emission toward high-mass protostars in W51 A, and where do they arise?

data.bands: ALMA Band 6 (1 mm) and Band 3 (3 mm); VLA Q-band (7 mm)
data.sensitivity: CS 2-1 0.59 mJy/beam (3 km/s channels); CS 1-0 1.3 mJy/beam (6 km/s)

what.value: Positions of OH, water and CH3OH masers for comparison

evidence.quote: The closest OH and water masers (cite: Fish2007a; Sato2010a) are separated by $>0.2\arcsec$ ($>1000$ AU).

recipe.method: Imaged CS J=2-1 (3 km/s channels, robust 0.5) and CS J=1-0 (6 km/s, robust 0) from calibrated data
Gaussian fits to line profiles and peak intensity images

recipe.goal: Infer enclosed mass from maser separation
recipe.method: Assume masers at opposite ends of an orbiting disk, v_orb=15 km/s, R=95 AU
assumptions: Masers trace orbiting material; invalid if from outflow

answer_key.quantity: CS 2-1 flux limit toward IRS2/North and e8

not_stated_but_needed: CASA version and tclean parameters (cell, image size, masks, niter, deconvolver)
Whether the VLA continuum band used for CS 1-0 was continuum-subtracted
ALMA configurations, baselines, and integration times
Details of the FK5-to-ICRS correction procedure
Gaussian fit method details for the line profiles
score_reason: Public data and key imaging weights are given, but CASA version and many imaging parameters are missing; the results are few.
rediscovery_reason: Data are public, imaging choices (robust, channel width) are stated, and the results are numeric line parameters.
